report.answer_text:
The Word of Wisdom became a formal commitment for Latter-day Saints on September 9, 1851, and a temple recommend requirement under President Heber J. Grant in the early 1920s. (churchofjesuschrist.org)
February 27, 1833: Joseph Smith received the revelation, now Doctrine and Covenants 89. It was originally given “not by commandment or constraint.” (churchofjesuschrist.org)
September 9, 1851: At general conference, members unanimously accepted Brigham Young’s proposal to covenant to keep it. In practice, expectations about strict observance still varied for decades. (churchofjesuschrist.org)
1919–1921: Official Church sources give different dates for the temple recommend requirement. The Church History Library dates it to 1919, while the Church’s *Church History Topics* dates it to 1921. (churchhistorylibrary.churchofjesuschrist.org)

quotes.text: On 9 September 1851, some eighteen years after it was given, the Patriarch to the Church, John Smith, delivered a talk in general conference on the Word of Wisdom.
President Brigham Young arose and proposed that all Saints formally covenant to abstain from tea, coffee, tobacco, whiskey, and “all things mentioned in the Word of Wisdom”
The motion was accepted unanimously and became binding as a commandment for all Church members thereafter.
